API plans and access

What each Consensus plan includes on the API: monthly calls, papers per request, pagination, full-text excerpts, complete text, citations, and rate limits.
The API is self-serve on every Consensus plan. Your plan sets how many calls you get each month, how many papers each request can return, and which features you can use.

Get a key

1. Open the dashboard
Sign in to Consensus and go to consensus.app/api-mcp, or click your profile icon and choose API & MCP Dashboard.
2. Create a key
Click Create API key, name it, and copy it. If you already have a key, open Keys and clients and click New key. The full key is shown once.
3. Send it on every request
Pass the key in the x-api-key header. Requests without a valid key return 401.

What each plan includes

*  | Free | Pro | Teams | Deep | Enterprise
* Included calls per month | 30 | 500 | 500 | 2,000 | Custom
* Max calls with additional usage | 30 | 1,000 | 1,000 | 10,000 | Custom
* Max papers per request (page_size) | 20 | 300 | 300 | 750 | 1,000
* Pagination past the first page | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes
* Full-text excerpts | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes
* Complete text of open-access papers** | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes
* Institutional full-text links (institutional_access_url)* | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes
* Citations and references (beta)*** | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes
* Rate limit | 1 request/second | 1 request/second | 1 request/second | 1 request/second | Custom

...

Enterprise

Enterprise adds custom call volumes and rate limits and up to 1,000 papers per request. An Enterprise contract covers search only: complete text, citations and references, and Threads are billed per credit at the standard rate, on top of the contract. Enterprise keys authenticate the same way as every other key: send them in the x-api-key header on requests to api.consensus.app.

Authorization: Bearer is for the MCP server (mcp.consensus.app/mcp), not the REST API. See MCP API key access.

excerpts:
# How to create an API key

You can create and manage API keys from the API & MCP Dashboard.

1. Click your profile icon (bottom-left corner)
2. Select **[API & MCP Dashboard](consensus.app/api-mcp/)**
3. Open the '**Keys and Clients**' tab
4. Click '**New key**'
5. Give your API key a name so you can identify what you're using it for
6. Create the key and copy it somewhere secure

Your full API key is only shown once. Make sure you copy it when you create it.

If you lose an API key, you won't be able to view it again. Instead, revoke the existing key and create a new one.

[](downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/wbmyui9a/2650022362/1ffde54676d37bedcf7f79ae633b/image.png?expires=1795270500&signature=1f124d3a479e7fdd1530f4598fb2e94dc6b4784ad145b5a35906499ca9a37d1f&req=diYiFsl8n4JZ…)

---

# Make your first API request

Once you've created an API key, you can use it to authenticate requests to the Consensus API.

To make a search request, you'll need three things:

1. The Consensus search endpoint: `api.consensus.app/v1/search`
2. Your API key, passed in the `x-api-key` request header
3. A `query` parameter containing what you want to search for

For example, if you want to search for research on whether creatine improves muscle strength, your request would send that question as the `query` to the Consensus search endpoint.

If you're using a tool such as Postman, a programming language, or another application to make the request, add your Consensus API key as an `x-api-key` header.

The API also supports filters that can help narrow your research, including publication date, study type, sample size, citation count, journal, academic field, country, open-access status, and more.

For request examples and a full list of available parameters and responses, see the [Consensus API Reference](docs.consensus.app/reference/v1_search).

...

# API and MCP usage limits

API and MCP usage share one monthly pool of calls.

| **Plan** | **Included calls per month** | **Maximum calls with additional usage ($0.05/call)** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Free** | 30 | 30 (no additional usage) |
| **Pro** | 500 | 1,000 |
| **Team** | 500 | 1,000 |
| **Enterprise** | 500 | 1,000 |
| **Deep** | 2,000 | 10,000 |

**Additional usage costs $0.05 per call** after you've used the calls included in your plan.

results.title: Connection reference
excerpts:
## Endpoint and transport

| | |
| - | - |
| **MCP endpoint** | `mcp.consensus.app/mcp` |
| **Transport** | Streamable HTTP |
| **Responses** | Buffered JSON. There is no SSE endpoint and the server never returns SSE event streams. |
| **Sessions** | Stateless. No `Mcp-Session-Id`, no session affinity, so your gateway needs no sticky-session configuration. |
| **Tools** | `search`, plus the thread tools `create_thread`, `get_thread`, `add_to_thread`, and `find_threads` for signed-in accounts and API keys, and `get_full_text` for paid plans. See the [tool reference](docs.consensus.app/mcp-tools/quickstart.md). |

> [!WARNING]
>
> All MCP and JSON-RPC calls must target the `/mcp` path. The bare host `mcp.consensus.app/` only answers health checks and OAuth discovery.

Where a product lets you choose a transport, pick **Streamable HTTP** explicitly. Some gateways default to SSE, which will fail against this server.

## Authentication

Two options. For a shared, server-side gateway credential, use an API key.

> [tab] API key (recommended for gateways)
>
> A single opaque credential sent as a bearer token:
>
> ```http theme={null}
> Authorization: Bearer ak_live_...
> ```
>
> It lives entirely server-side, involves no user redirect and no token refresh, and maps to your Enterprise tier. Generate one from your Consensus account: profile icon → **API & MCP Dashboard** → **Keys and clients** → **New key**. The full key is shown once.
>
> Treat it like a password: keep it out of client-side code, public repositories, and screenshots.

> [tab] OAuth 2.0 (per-user)
>
> Authorization-code flow only. There is no client-credentials grant, so OAuth always involves a per-user consent step; each user signs in to their own Consensus account.
>
> | | |
> | - | - |
> | **Authorization URL** | `consensus.app/oauth/authorize/` |
> | **Token URL** | `consensus.app/oauth/token/` |
> | **Dynamic Client Registration** | `consensus.app/oauth/register/` (RFC 7591) |
> | **Scope** | `search`. Request `scope=search` or omit it; it's the default. This is not an OIDC provider, so there are no `openid` or `email` scopes. |
> | **PKCE** | Required.

results.title: API
excerpts:
API

The Consensus API lets you integrate research search into your own applications, agents, and workflows. One REST endpoint, 400 million papers, self-serve keys.
The Consensus API puts Consensus search inside your own applications, tools, and workflows. Send a query, get back ranked peer-reviewed papers with metadata, and skip running each search by hand.
The API is self-serve and open to everyone.
GET api.consensus.app/v1/search
Authentication, your first request in cURL, Python, JavaScript, and Go, and the full parameter reference.

What you get

...

Get a key

Click your profile icon in the bottom-left of Consensus and choose **API & MCP Dashboard**.
Open the **Keys and Clients** tab, click **New key**, and name it.
The full key is shown once. If you lose it, revoke it and create a new one.
Send the key in the x-api-key header on every request. Treat it like a password: keep it out of client-side code, public repositories, and screenshots.

Plans and limits

API and MCP calls share one monthly pool.
* Plan | Included calls per month | Max with additional usage | Max papers per call
* Free | 30 | 30 | 20
* Pro | 500 | 1,000 | 300
* Teams | 500 | 1,000 | 300
* Enterprise | Custom | Custom | 1,000
* Deep | 2,000 | 10,000 | 750
* A call covers up to 100 papers, rounded up, with a minimum of 1 call per request.
* Additional usage costs $0.05 per call. It's off by default; enable it in the dashboard. Free plans can't enable it.
* Rate limit: 1 request per second (custom on Enterprise).
* A query returns at most 1,000 results in total across pages.
* Usage resets on the 1st of each month.
See API plans and access for pagination, errors, and Enterprise details.

Common errors

* Status | Meaning
* 401 | Invalid or revoked key, or missing x-api-key header
* 402 | Billing past due — calls pause until payment is resolved
* 429 "used all included searches" | Monthly pool exhausted; resets on the date shown
* 429 "Too many requests" | More than 1 request per second
Need higher limits? Contact [sales@consensus.app](mailto:sales@consensus.app) about Enterprise access. Enterprise keys also use the `x-api-key` header. Bearer-token auth (`Authorization: Bearer`) applies only to the [MCP server](/mcp-plans-and-access#api-key-access).

Getting Started with the Consensus MCP

The Consensus MCP server enables AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude, and other MCP-compatible clients to search over 200 million peer-reviewed academic research papers directly from the conversation.

Getting Started

Consensus MCP lets AI assistants search 200+ million peer-reviewed research papers. Connect your preferred client below — you'll be searching in under 2 minutes.
Server URL: mcp.consensus.app/mcp
The /mcp path is required. Using mcp.consensus.app alone will not work.

...

1. Connect the Consensus app in ChatGPT using the steps above
2. Start a Deep Research request in ChatGPT
3. Ask ChatGPT to use Consensus for peer-reviewed research, for example:
Use Consensus to research the evidence on exercise for depression. Prioritize systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and randomized controlled trials.
Deep Research may run multiple Consensus searches, refine filters, fetch paper details, and return a cited synthesis with direct links to papers on Consensus.
The fetch tool used by Deep Research is currently available for ChatGPT only. Other MCP clients use the search tool.

Claude Code

Bash
claude mcp add --transport http consensus mcp.consensus.app/mcp
OAuth will open in your browser automatically on first use. You can also trigger it manually with the /mcp command inside Claude Code.

Codex

Bash
codex mcp add consensus --url mcp.consensus.app/mcp
codex mcp login consensus

Cursor

...

Enterprise and API Key Access

For enterprise access with unlimited rate limits, include your API key as a Bearer token:
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY
Contact Consensus for enterprise API access at consensus.app/home/api .

Search Tool

The search tool searches Consensus for peer-reviewed research papers. ChatGPT Deep Research may call this tool multiple times with different queries and filters while building a research report.

Parameters

* Parameter | Type | Required | Description
* query | string | Yes | The research question or topic to search for. Use specific academic terminology for best results.
* year_min | integer | No | Exclude papers published before this year.
* year_max | integer | No | Exclude papers published after this year.
* study_types | string array | No | Filter by study design. Values: rct , meta-analysis , systematic review , literature review , case report , non-rct experimental , non-rct observational study , non-rct in vitro , animal .

results.title: Use Consensus in ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, or with the API
excerpts:
Using a different assistant or tool, such as Cursor, VS Code, or Claude Code? Connect it to the Consensus MCP server directly. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standard way for AI assistants to use outside tools. The server is hosted, so there's nothing to install:
mcp.consensus.app/mcp
[card] Set up your client
Step-by-step connection guides for Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Gemini Spark, Copilot Studio, and any other MCP client.

What your assistant can do

Search. The search tool returns ranked papers with title, authors, journal, publication year, citation count, study type, a key takeaway, and a link to the paper on Consensus. On paid plans it also returns query-relevant excerpts from open-access papers, so your assistant can quote the passage behind each claim. Your assistant can pass the same filters Research Agent uses:

...

Consensus publishes prompt templates ("skills") for common research jobs you can run through MCP:
* Literature review helper — reconnaissance, PICO/SPIDER decomposition, systematic searching, and synthesis.
* Curriculum development — parse a syllabus into a reading list with discussion questions.
* Grant research — position your idea, map it to NIH institutes and mechanisms, and find funded overlap.
See Skills, or browse the full gallery in Use cases.

Use the API

Building your own tool, agent, or workflow? The Consensus API gives you the same paper search over REST, and can run Research Agent as a Thread. Send a query, get back ranked peer-reviewed papers with metadata, and skip running each search by hand. It's self-serve and open to everyone.
GET api.consensus.app/v1/search
* The top 20 most relevant papers per query by default; raise page_size for more, up to your plan's maximum
* Metadata on every paper: title, authors, journal, year, DOI, citation count, and a link
* On paid plans: study design, journal rank, key takeaways, and query-relevant excerpts from open-access papers
* The same filters as the web app: publication date, study type, sample size, citations, journal quality, field, country, and open access
To get a key, click your profile icon in Consensus, choose API & MCP Dashboard, open Keys and Clients, and click New key.
[card] Get started with the API
Authentication, your first request, and the full parameter reference.
[card] Run Research Agent from code
Start a Thread, wait for the cited answer, and ask follow-ups.

Plans and limits

API and MCP calls share one monthly pool.
* Plan | Max papers per call | Included calls per month | Rate limit | Extra fields
* No account | 3 | No monthly limit | 5 per second, shared | —
* Free | 10 | 30 | 1 per second | —
* Pro | 300 | 500 | 3 per second | Study type, takeaway, DOI
* Deep | 750 | 2,000 | 3 per second | Study type, takeaway, DOI
* Teams | 300 | 500 | 3 per second | Study type, takeaway, DOI
* Enterprise | 1,000 | Custom | Custom | Study type, takeaway, DOI
* A call covers up to 100 papers: 1–100 papers is 1 call, 101–200 is 2, and so on. Requests default to 20 papers.
* Paid plans can enable additional usage at $0.05 per call, up to 1,000 calls per month (10,000 on Deep). It's off by default.
* Usage resets on the 1st of each month.
See MCP plans and access for the full breakdown.
Track usage, connected clients, and billing from your profile icon under API & MCP Dashboard.
<The API & MCP Dashboard's Keys and clients tab listing Claude and ChatGPT as connected MCP clients>
Connected MCP clients appear under Keys and clients, alongside your API keys.
[!NOTE]
Clients without OAuth can pass any Consensus API key as a Bearer token. The key gets its owner's plan limits. See MCP plans and access. For custom Enterprise limits, contact sales@consensus.app.

sources.title: Consensus: AI for Research
sources.trimmed:
# Research starts here

---

## The new standard for academic research

---

Search and analyze peer-reviewed literature. Consensus draws on 400M scholarly works, including licensed full text content from leading publishers.

See all publisher partners

---

## Used daily at top research institutions

---

Over 170 university libraries partner with Consensus to give students and faculty access. 10 million researchers, students, and clinicians use Consensus to supercharge literature reviews — without sacrificing academic rigor.

---

---

## Automate Literature Review with Deep Search

Turn days of literature review into a few minutes. Consensus Deep Search builds a comprehensive search strategy, expanding key terms, identifying conflicting arguments, and exploring the citation graph.

---

## Try Medical mode

Narrow your results to the highest-quality medical sources — about 50,000 clinical guidelines and 8M articles from the top 1,000 medical journals for quick, trusted clinical answers.

---

## Use filters with natural language

Specify timeframes, populations, designs, and more directly in your prompt — and Consensus automatically applies the right filters for your search.

---

## See where the research agrees

Ask a clear yes-or-no research question and the Consensus Meter instantly shows how much the evidence agrees or disagrees — giving you a fast, visual read on the state of the research.

| Max papers per request (`page_size`) | 20 | 300 | 300 | 750 | 1,000 |
| Pagination past the first page | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Full-text excerpts | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Complete text of open-access papers\*\* | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

\*\* `GET /v1/papers/full_text`, at 1 credit per paper returned.

Every plan can use every search filter. Compare plans at consensus.app/pricing.

## How calls are counted

* **One call per 100 papers returned**, rounded up, with a minimum of one call per request. A request that returns 20 papers is 1 call; 150 papers is 2 calls.
* **A Thread is charged by the amount of work the agent does.** `mode` controls the effort: a `deep` run does more work than a `pro` run, so it costs more. A failed run costs nothing. While a Thread runs, its maximum possible cost counts as used. If that doesn’t fit under your plan’s limit, creating the Thread or adding a follow-up returns `429`.
* **One credit per full text returned.** Complete text costs 1 credit for each paper whose Markdown comes back, and a credit counts the same as a call. Papers that come back blocked or not found cost nothing. A paper charged to you in the last 24 hours, through the API or MCP, normally comes back free.
* **One credit per 100 citing or cited papers returned.** `GET /v1beta/papers/citations` and `GET /v1beta/papers/references` are charged by the papers on the page, rounded up, with a minimum of 1 credit per request.
* **API and MCP share one monthly pool.** Searches from your API key and from your MCP connection draw down the same allowance.
* **Usage resets on the 1st of each month.** Track it in the **Usage** tab of the API & MCP Dashboard.

### Additional usage

Pro, Teams, and Deep can keep making calls past the included amount, up to the plan’s maximum, at **$0.05 per call**. Additional usage is off by default; turn it on in the API & MCP Dashboard. Free plans stop at 30 calls.

* **`page_size` defaults to 20.** A larger value is capped to your plan’s maximum rather than rejected, so check the `page_size` echoed in the response.
* **Pages are zero-indexed.** Requesting `page=1` or later needs a paid plan; on Free it returns `403`.
* **A query returns at most 1,000 results in total.** `(page + 1) × page_size` can’t exceed 1,000 on any plan. With `page_size=250`, pages 0–3 cover the full 1,000. To go wider, split the topic into narrower queries or tighter filters.

The Consensus API lets you search 400+ million scholarly articles, including 350 million peer-reviewed research papers, over a single REST endpoint. Send a query and get back ranked papers with titles, authors, journals, publication years, citation counts, and direct links.

## Quickstart

Make your first API call in a few minutes. Every plan includes API access, and the Free plan includes 30 calls a month.

1

Sign in to Consensus

Create a free account or sign in at consensus.app. The dashboard in the next step only opens when you’re signed in.

2

Open the API & MCP Dashboard

Go to consensus.app/api-mcp. You can also get there from your profile icon: choose **API & MCP Dashboard**.

3

Create and copy an API key

Click **Create API key**, name the key, and click **Copy API key**. The full key is shown only once, so store it somewhere safe.Already have a key? Open **Keys and clients** and click **New key**.

4

Make your first request

Save the key in an environment variable named `CONSENSUS_API_KEY`:

```
export CONSENSUS_API_KEY="paste-your-key-here"
```

```
curl "https://api.consensus.app/v1/search?query=creatine%20and%20cognitive%20function" \
  -H "x-api-key: $CONSENSUS_API_KEY"
```

No account is needed to get started. Connect directly and try it out, then sign in for more results per search.

## What each plan includes

|  | No account | Free | Pro | Teams | Deep | Enterprise |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Papers per search | 3 | 10 | Up to 300 | Up to 300 | Up to 750 | Up to 1,000 |

| Rate limit | 5 requests/second, shared by all no-account users | 1 request/second | 3 requests/second | 3 requests/second | 3 requests/second | Custom |
| Study type, takeaway, and DOI in results | No | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Pagination past the first page | No | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Full-text excerpts | No | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Complete text of open-access papers | No | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Institutional full-text links\* | No | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

\* Returned on the first 50 results when you’ve selected your institution in Consensus settings. An organization key uses the institution of the person who created it.
Create a free account at consensus.app/sign-up or upgrade at consensus.app/pricing.

## How calls are counted

* **One call per 100 papers returned**, rounded up, with a minimum of one call per request. A search that returns 150 papers uses 2 calls.
* **A Thread is charged by the amount of work the agent does.** `mode` controls the effort: a `deep` run does more work than a `pro` run, so it costs more. A failed run costs nothing. While a Thread runs, its maximum possible cost counts as used. If that doesn’t fit under your plan’s limit, starting the Thread or adding a follow-up returns an error.
* **One credit per full text returned.** `get_full_text` costs 1 credit for each paper whose text comes back, and a credit counts the same as a call. Papers that come back blocked or not found cost nothing. A paper charged to you in the last 24 hours normally comes back free, so continuing a long paper with its cursor usually costs nothing.
* **MCP and API share one monthly pool.** Searches from your MCP connection and from your API key draw down the same allowance.
* **Usage resets on the 1st of each month.**

“Papers per search” is the per-request ceiling. Searches that don’t set a page size still return the default of 20 papers, or your plan’s cap if it’s lower.

### Additional usage

Pro, Teams, and Deep can keep making calls past the included amount, up to the plan’s maximum, when the account has an active metered API subscription and additional usage is turned on. Additional usage is billed at **$0.05 per call**. Free plans stop at 30 calls.

## API key access

Any Consensus API key works on the MCP server. Include it as a Bearer token and the server applies the key owner’s plan: a personal key gets your plan, and an organization key gets that organization’s plan. Enterprise keys get custom limits.

```
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY
```

See API key (Bearer token) for example client configs.

# How to create an API key

You can create and manage API keys from the API & MCP Dashboard.

1. Click your profile icon (bottom-left corner)
2. Select **[API & MCP Dashboard](consensus.app/api-mcp/)**
3. Open the '**Keys and Clients**' tab
4. Click '**New key**'
5. Give your API key a name so you can identify what you're using it for
6. Create the key and copy it somewhere secure

Your full API key is only shown once. Make sure you copy it when you create it.

If you lose an API key, you won't be able to view it again. Instead, revoke the existing key and create a new one.
